p4a: One place to look is the parent you inherited. I mean the way you learned to treat yourself from how people treated you growing up, long before you started building the Nurturer, Protector and Guide. For some people it's warm. For a lot of people it starts out as a critic. Or a warden, with rules like don't cry, don't be needy, don't get angry, don't embarrass us, don't get too independent. If yours was like that, your little one learned bit by bit to hide the crying and the anger so they could keep belonging. And the wanting too, and whatever embarrassed the family.
p4b: When it feels fake, I'd look at the parent you inherited. I mean the way you learned to treat yourself from how people treated you growing up, long before the Nurturer, Protector and Guide came along. For some people it's warm. For a lot of people it starts out as a critic or a warden, with rules: don't cry, don't be needy, don't get angry, don't embarrass us, don't get too independent. If that's you, your little one learned bit by bit to hide what those rules didn't allow, so they could keep belonging. The crying and the anger, but also the wanting, and whatever embarrassed the family.
p4c: When you look into why it feels fake, I'd start with the parent you inherited. I mean the way you learned to treat yourself from how people treated you growing up, long before your Nurturer, Protector and Guide. For some people it's warm. For a lot of people, though, it starts out as a critic or a warden, with rules like don't cry, don't be needy, don't get angry, don't embarrass us, don't get too independent. Where it was like that, your little one learned bit by bit to keep belonging by hiding the crying and the anger, but also the wanting, and whatever embarrassed the family.
p6a: The new grown-up could start as something other than a voice, though: a person who likes you the way you are, or a plan you wrote down on a calmer day, or one small thing you actually do to protect your little one. None of those waits for an answer or asks you to fake a feeling. They can earn trust by showing up again and again, even while the parent you inherited is still calling them fake.
p6b: Saying yes would mean faking a feeling, but the new grown-up can help without that, and without winning the argument where the parent you inherited calls it fake. It doesn't have to start as a voice, either: someone who likes you the way you are can earn trust by showing up again and again, and so can a plan you wrote down on a calmer day, or one small thing you actually do to protect your little one.
p6c: The new grown-up can start outside your head, though, as someone who likes you the way you are, a plan you wrote down on a calmer day, or one small thing you actually do to protect your little one. None of those wait for an answer before they help, or ask you for a feeling you don't have. I think they earn trust by showing up again and again, while the parent you inherited still argues they're fake.
